scenario: My mentor, who used to respond to my messages almost instantly, has ignored my last three informal check-in requests. They still participate actively in our department meetings and appear highly engaged with the rest of the team. When I last reached out to schedule a brief sync, they replied with a short 'not right now' and did not suggest an alternative time.
reading1: they are testing my ability to work autonomously and make decisions without their constant oversight
reading2: they are dissatisfied with my recent professional progress and are distancing themselves from our mentorship
reading3: they are struggling with an intense workload or personal matter that has left them with zero capacity for extra meetings

scenario: Alex cancelled our lunch date today via a brief text, saying he couldn't make it. He didn't offer a reason or suggest a time to reschedule. When I saw him in the hallway later, he gave me a quick wave but didn't stop to talk.
reading1: he is going through a personal crisis and is withdrawing from everyone
reading2: he is upset with me and is intentionally giving me the cold shoulder
reading3: he is just overwhelmed with work and is being unintentionally flaky

scenario: I've spent ten years training for the residency I always wanted, but now that I'm finally here, I feel a profound sense of detachment during my rounds. I find myself observing my colleagues' passion with a clinical curiosity rather than sharing it. The goals I once cherished now feel like instructions left by a stranger.
reading1: I have outgrown my youthful idealism and am evolving into a more pragmatic, professional version of myself
reading2: I have spent years chasing a goal that never truly aligned with my core identity and it is time to pivot
reading3: I am experiencing severe burnout that has temporarily severed my emotional connection to my passion

scenario: My director just added me to the executive steering committee meeting tomorrow without any prior discussion. She didn't include an agenda, and my peer, who usually handles these, is on vacation. I haven't received any feedback on my latest project milestones.
reading1: she is giving me a chance to showcase my work and step up in my peer's absence
reading2: she just needs someone to take minutes and provide administrative support while my peer is out
reading3: there is a critical issue with my project that the executives want addressed immediately

scenario: We used to grab coffee every morning, but lately, they only speak to me when it's strictly about work tasks. When I try to make small talk, they give brief, polite responses and quickly return to their screen. They still attend our team lunches, but they now sit at the far end of the table.
reading1: they are angry with me and are using professional distance to express their frustration
reading2: they are going through a difficult personal time and are minimizing all social interaction
reading3: they have decided to transition our relationship from a friendship to a strictly professional one

scenario: After ten years of relentless auditions, I finally secured a permanent seat in the metropolitan symphony I spent my entire youth aiming for. Yet as I sat in the rehearsal hall this morning tuning my cello, a heavy numbness replaced the euphoria I had expected. When the conductor congratulated me on finally reaching my lifelong home, I felt an overwhelming urge to pack my instrument and walk out.
reading1: this emptiness is merely the psychological anti-climax of achieving a long-term milestone, so I should stay put and give myself time to adjust
reading2: this ambition was an unexamined identity built purely for external validation, so I should walk away and figure out who I actually am
reading3: my core musicianship is genuine but fundamentally incompatible with a rigid orchestral hierarchy, so I should resign and pursue an independent creative path

scenario: My director sent me a calendar invite for tomorrow's executive leadership meeting without any agenda or context. My direct manager hasn't mentioned it, and I am the only non-manager on the guest list. The meeting is titled 'Organizational Alignment'.
reading1: I'm being fast-tracked for a promotion and they want to gauge my presence in a high-level environment
reading2: I'm being let go or moved due to restructuring and they want the full chain of command present
reading3: I'm being brought in as a subject matter expert to clarify a specific technical point for the executives
